$comment: Permissions for loop-triage runs. Triage is 'read-only' with respect to code,
but it holds the Projects PAT and reads untrusted text — issue titles and
bodies off the board — so it is prompt-injection reachable and needs real
rules, not just a job description.
The dangerous surface is `gh api`: the PAT carries Workflows write, so an
unrestricted gh would let triage PUT a new .github/workflows/*.yml onto main.
There is no gate step in the triage workflow to catch that afterwards.
Triage writes exactly three kinds of thing: avengers-12/state/STATE.md, issue labels, and the
Loop Queue dashboard issue. Everything else is denied.
git is denied WHOLESALE. Triage does not need it: the queue comes from `gh`,
and the one git command it used to run — `git log origin/main` — could not
work anyway, because the job checks out a single ref at depth 50 and
origin/main may not be there. Denying the whole verb closes the spelling gap:
the rules are prefix matches, so `Bash(git push:*)` alone never stopped
`git -C . push` or `env GIT_DIR=.git git push`. Note that deny beats allow, so
there is no way to deny `git` and allow `git log` back — which is exactly why
the skill was changed to stop asking for it.
Reading .git/ is denied too. The triage checkout now runs with
persist-credentials: false so the PAT should not be in .git/config at all;
this is the second lock on the same door.
Card movement is NOT triage's job and is denied here. Columns are moved by
bash — preflight to In Progress, the PR step to In Review, escalate to
Blocked, the pull_request:closed workflow to Done — so a card's position
always reflects what a run actually did, not what a model believed. The allow
list below is read-only on purpose; the explicit project denies matter because
claude_args grants bare Bash, and without them 'not in the allow list' would
not have meant 'blocked'.
